scenes.heading: Primes and prime factorisation
scenes.sub: The building blocks of every whole number
scenes.say: Every whole number bigger than one can be built by multiplying special numbers called primes. In this video you'll learn what primes are and how to break any number down into them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Lego models are built from small bricks that can't be split
scenes.science: Every number is built by multiplying primes: 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5
scenes.breaks: Lego bricks stack side by side, but prime factors are multiplied, not added.
scenes.say: Think of primes as tiny Lego bricks that can't be pulled apart. Every other number is a model built from them. Sixty is built from two, two, three and five, multiplied together. However you take it apart, you always get the same bricks.
scenes.caption: Think of primes as tiny Lego bricks that can't be pulled apart. Every other number is a model built from them. 60 is built from 2, 2, 3 and 5, multiplied together. However you take it apart, you always get the same bricks.

scenes.heading: Prime or composite?
points: Prime: exactly two factors, 1 and itself
1 is neither; 2 is the only even prime
scenes.say: A prime has exactly two factors: one and itself. The primes up to thirty are two, three, five, seven, eleven, thirteen, seventeen, nineteen, twenty-three and twenty-nine. A composite number has more than two factors. One is neither prime nor composite, and two is the only even prime.

scenes.heading: Making a factor tree
steps: Write the number at the top
Split it into a factor pair
Keep splitting until all are prime
scenes.say: To make a factor tree, write the number at the top. Split it into any factor pair. Keep splitting each branch until every end is a prime. Then write the primes multiplied together, from smallest to largest.

scenes.heading: A factor tree for 60
notes: Circle the primes at the ends
scenes.say: Here's a factor tree for sixty. First sixty splits into six times ten. Then six splits into two times three, and ten into two times five. The circled primes give sixty equals two times two times three times five.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Write 72 as a product of prime factors.
scenes.say: Let's write seventy-two as a product of primes. Split it into eight times nine. Eight is two times two times two. Nine is three times three. So seventy-two equals two times two times two times three times three. Check by multiplying back: eight times nine is seventy-two.

scenes.heading: Watch out
scenes.say: Watch out for numbers that look prime but aren't. One has only one factor. Fifty-one is three times seventeen, and ninety-one is seven times thirteen. Meanwhile two, fifty-three and forty-seven really are prime. Always test with two, three, five and seven.

points: 1 is not prime; 2 is the only even prime
scenes.say: Quick recap. Primes have exactly two factors. One is not prime, and two is the only even prime. Factor trees keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime. And always multiply back to check. Now try the practice questions!
